title: Capability records used in the manuscript (scope-limited derivative)
scope: UR3: demonstrated interaction, timing definitions and commanded responses to injected inputs. UR5: source-linked capability records, including the earlier team account in records/UR5_OPERATION_CLARIFICATION.json. The later summary of the developer's answers takes precedence where the accounts differ. G1: original records unchanged. Omitted UR3 questions are not reclassified as supported.
original_record_status: The complete historical record and later errata remain preserved with the authors, outside this publication candidate.

records.capability: Soft-stop response to an injected trigger
records.value: Logged post-limiter command in the illustrated soft-stop episode: it ramps down from 0.1485 rad/s at latch entry (initial changes −0.015 rad/s per tick), is at most 0.05 rad/s from about 0.35 s after entry and stays within that bound until release. The published Figure 11 window (released log data rows 4619–4679, header excluded) shows 0.03–0.13 rad/s logged post-limiter command, including transition samples, and up to 2.25 rad/s raw command.
records.evidence_scope: Released command log (slew_log.csv, SHA256 14928763aff0b9d63a4202c27fe091b6dd9bdd5b0098041a91e8160e285edcd0, bound to the archived public repository tree at src/report/data/slew_log.csv); keyboard-triggered trial-day soft-stops. The Figure 11 window holds 59 active-latch samples and 2 post-release samples; the active latch is data rows 4618–4677 (60 samples; header excluded).
records.limits: Commanded values, not measured robot speed; not a certified safety function. The logged command stays above 0.05 rad/s for the first 0.35 s of the latch while it falls by 0.015 rad/s per tick, so 0.05 rad/s is not an instantaneous bound on the outgoing command throughout the latch. The trial-day controller executable is not independently reconstructed.
records.source: Released UR3 command log (slew_log.csv) and the published Figure 11 of Goonetilleke and Khalid (2026). Every retained value is computed from the log (records/CASE_RECORDS_README.md).
